page.layout: One page of text. Running head and page number at the top. Below the running head, a centred italic subtitle. Then a three-column table of numbers with a sentence above and a result table below, a paragraph of explanation, and a worked sum with a cross at the right. No margin notes.

main_text.l: Prima vice | Secunda vice | Tertia vice
main_text.p: Quæritur quot Thaleros, Albos, & Nu-mulos expofuetit? per additionem nume-ris collectis proveniunt
Si scire cupio, an rectè numeros per ad-ditionem collegerim, 9. à toto numero supra lineam posito, quoties potero abjicio, & quicquid novenario minus remanserit supra literam X colloco.
Deinde ex numero sub linea 9 rejicio, & si hæc nota, quæ remanet, eadem est, quæ supra literam X posita fuit, rectè operatus sum,hoc modo:

page.notes: The sums in the first table are set with spaces between the digits (for example "4 3", "1 6 2", "2 5") in the printed type; I have written them as the two- or three-digit numbers they are, since the column totals (236, 43, 52) confirm the values. The "ct" ligature in "colleētis" is hard to read; I have not reproduced it with certainty. The old-style numerals of the worked addition (rows of symbols and the result line) are not legible enough to copy letter by letter. The cross at the right has small "o" marks above and below the X; these are part of the diagram, not text.
